pages.title: What it does
text: It drives the vanilla minecraft:armor attribute inside the vanilla armor pipeline (before resistance and Protection).

Armor points are not a damage reduction percentage. The vanilla formula is: reduction = clamp( clamp(A - D / (2 + T/4), A * 0.2, 20), 0, 25 ) / 25, where A is armor, T is armor toughness and D is the incoming damage.

Because the formula clamps effective armor to 20, armor alone can never reduce more than 20/25 = 80%, and the harder you are hit the more of it is eroded. With 20 armor and no toughness: 40% reduction against a 20 damage hit, only 16% against 40 or more.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +0.15 armor points per point, with no diminishing returns.
The old curve, gain = 6 * x / (x + 40), had an initial slope of exactly 6/40 = 0.15, so the first points pay exactly what they always did - they simply never converge now.

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: 1.666667 per point, on the DESIGN_BASELINE basis with reference B_ref = 4.0 armor points.
It does not scale the live attribute, which is why it still pays out on a naked character.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: The armor attribute caps at 30 (an attribute-range mod such as AttributeFix raises that automatically). Both lines are linear, so points climb all the way to 30: the flat line alone reaches +30 at 200 points, which already fills a naked character.

Past the ceiling vanilla sanitizeValue silently discards the excess. This mod reports that fact instead of hiding it: the row shows a "!" marker and stat.armor.clamped reads true. That is the price of removing diminishing returns, not a defect.

A second, independent ceiling lives in the damage formula: effective armor is clamped to 20, so for single hits up to roughly 70 damage, armor above 20 buys almost nothing unless you also have armor toughness.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: Armor should mostly come from gear; spend points on armor toughness and damage reduction instead.
If you already wear full netherite (gear holds 20 of the 30), only 10 points of headroom remain, and 200 flat points fill it.
With an attribute-range mod (AttributeFix) that headroom grows together with the attribute, and no configuration changes are needed.
